verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Term for term identical: coefficient 1 on A_R^2, coefficient 1/2 on E_R', 1/2 on both the Laplacian and the transport term, 1 on the pressure term, and the transport field in the third term is v (the second solution), as in the paper. Two routine rewritings. (i) Sign convention: the paper sets w = v - u and π = P - p, the Lean uses w_L = u - v and π_L = p - q, so w_L = -w and π_L = -π; every term of the identity is jointly even in (w, π) — the first three are quadratic in w, and the fourth is bilinear in (π, w) — so the identity is unchanged. (ii) The Lean states it for an arbitrary smooth compactly supported scalar χ rather than only for χ_R = φ_R^8; instantiating χ := ComparisonCutoffs.weight R (verified to be cutoff R ^ 8 with cutoff R x = φ(x/R)) gives the paper's display. Lean's weightedEnergyRate is shown to be the derivative of weightedEnergy by weightedEnergy_hasDerivAt (line 74), so (1/2)*weightedEnergyRate is the paper's (1/2)E_R'.
